indicators.note: the agent word takes the tip word inside it, so one sits within the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
in racing tipsters' columns the NAP is the day's most confident tip

explanation.surface: A spy with a bad temper let slip a valuable piece of inside information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' puts NAP inside SPY. A nap is the racing tipster's best bet of the day, a British newspaper convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy describes someone irritable who answers sharply, so it is a synonym for short-tempered.

clue.text: Old scholar found rudimentary dwelling in southeast

indicators.note: the dwelling word goes inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: a crib is a hut or hovel, a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A learned man of old was discovered living in a hut in the south east.
explanation.definitionFit: In biblical times a scribe was a scholar and teacher of the law, a learned man of old.

definitions.meaning: a large seabird of southern oceans
in golf, three strokes under par on one hole

explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a seabird; in golf it names a score three under par, beyond an eagle.

clue.text: Lead about alternative vegetable for flavouring

indicators.note: about means around, so the metal symbol goes round the other word

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
other means alternative, as in the other option

explanation.surface: A leaden alternative to a seasoning vegetable is proposed.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is any leafy plant grown for the pot as a vegetable or for seasoning.

definitions.meaning: not keeping a lookout, as a sentry off duty

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone unprepared, their alertness relaxed and not keeping watch.

indicators.note: the notices come after teatime in this down clue

parts.note: four o'clock is the traditional British teatime
posters are printed notices

explanation.surface: Notices go up after the afternoon tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-poster is a bed with a post at each corner, often hung with curtains.

indicators.note: during puts the excess abbreviation in the middle of the giving word

parts.note: gave means donated
OTT stands for over the top, too much

explanation.surface: Someone gave far too generously at a dance fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, short for over the top, is common British shorthand for excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French dance in moderate four-four time.

indicators.note: fermenting means bubbling and working, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Yeast that is still fermenting in a brew.
explanation.definitionFit: As yet means up to now, the same as still in the sense of so far.

clue.text: Mad having called during the action

indicators.note: during puts the telephoning word inside the action word

parts.note: a deed is an action
rang means called on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone went mad when a phone call came in the middle of the action.
explanation.definitionFit: Deranged means mentally disturbed, a synonym of mad.

clue.text: Discount as leaving new base rate

indicators.note: the letters of the little word as are left out of the mixture
new signals that the remaining letters of base rate are made into something fresh

parts.note: taken as written as the pool of letters
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A bank cuts its customers a deal while setting a new central interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: BASE RATE minus A and S leaves BERATE, which 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is money returned to a payer, a form of discount on the amount charged.

indicators.note: dithery means jittery and unsettled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An official inspecting the property is grumpy and indecisive.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor examines buildings or land and reports on their condition, an inspector by trade.

clue.text: Bloomer getting prize at dairy show

parts.note: butter is a typical dairy product
a cup is a trophy awarded as a prize

explanation.surface: Someone wins a trophy at an agricultural dairy exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder or a loaf, but here it means a flower, something that blooms. 'getting', 'at' and 'show' only join the picture of a cup won at a dairy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a yellow wild flower, and a flower is jokily a bloomer, something that blooms.

clue.text: Criminal made an effort despite being shackled

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
strained means tried hard

explanation.surface: A convict tried hard even with his chains on.
explanation.definitionFit: Constrained means restricted or held back, as someone shackled is.

clue.text: One in island race, a new giant

indicators.note: the letter for one is put inside the race abbreviation

parts.note: the TT is the motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A newcomer competing in the Isle of Man motorbike race turns out to be a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant deities of Greek myth, so the word now means any giant.

indicators.note: depicting suggests the letters are rearranged to portray something else

explanation.surface: A Swiss holiday postcard shows a picture of royal finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is only a link: the anagram uses just BERNE POSTCARD, which has thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The orb and the sceptre are items of the monarch's ceremonial regalia carried at coronations.

clue.text: Sit down, assume one's to have a meal

parts.note: to take on a role is to assume it
one is A, and the apostrophe s adds S
to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: A host invites a guest to settle in and assume they are staying for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a seat is the polite idiom for sitting down.

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to extract or remove one thing from another
a short statement of a paper's main points

explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to separate or withdraw; an abstract is also a summary of a document.

parts.note: beside means next to, near
the is the definite article
a mark is a spot or blemish

explanation.surface: Something close to an exact location is judged of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a remark beside the mark misses the point, so it is irrelevant.

indicators.note: out of here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Help Father climb out of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is a salt lake between Israel and Jordan, despite its name.

clue.text: Stupid like one over the eight

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
the Roman numeral for one is I
the number one more than eight is nine

explanation.surface: Being drunk is idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for slightly drunk, which disguises the split into ONE and OVER THE EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish, literally like an ass, a synonym for stupid.

clue.text: Sister going round gallery found old Greek coin

indicators.note: the sister abbreviation goes around the gallery name

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviation for Sister, as for a nun
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A nun touring an art gallery comes across an ancient coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries, the best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The stater was a gold or silver coin used in ancient Greece.

indicators.note: put back means the run of letters is turned round end to end

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A top-quality fragment of bone is returned to its place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns the whole of AIBIT backwards; the 1 of A1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: Endlessly courageous going over a Spanish Costa

indicators.note: in a down clue the shortened word sits above the letter A
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: brave means courageous

explanation.surface: A brave traveller crosses a Spanish holiday coast without end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Costa Brava is the Catalan coast of Spain, so Brava is the name of that Spanish Costa.

indicators.note: savaging means mauling, so the letters are torn apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: German shepherd dogs maul someone who goes for them.
explanation.walkthrough: An Alsatian is the British name for a German shepherd dog.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is a person who assaults another, a direct synonym for attacker.

clue.text: Gathering at a church service in German

parts.note: Mass is the Eucharist service in the Catholic church

explanation.surface: Someone attends a church service conducted in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Amassing means collecting or accumulating, the same as gathering in its verbal sense.

parts.note: grammar contrasts reported speech, which paraphrases, with the kind that quotes a speaker word for word

explanation.definitionFit: Direct speech quotes the actual words spoken, as opposed to reported or indirect speech.

clue.text: Edward accepting accountant had container for drinks

indicators.note: the name takes the accountant abbreviation inside it, as if receiving it

parts.note: Teddy is a pet form of the name Edward
ACA stands for Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants

explanation.surface: A man named Edward took on a bookkeeper who owned a drinks box.
explanation.walkthrough: ACA, a chartered accountant's qualification, goes in after the first two letters; 'had' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a tin or box for storing tea leaves, the makings of a drink.

parts.note: personnel are staff, men
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A guide leads staff down to the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is an experienced adviser who guides a less experienced person.
